description:
The Results Explorer UAT sweep found cells that were recorded as passed even
though the run log reported query-level failures. Examples include
`spark_tpchavoc_0.1_20260502_205516.log:5910`, which reported 203 passed and
17 failed queries, and `pandas-df_read_primitives_1.0_20260502_211633.log:145`,
which reported completion with failures.

A cell should not be eligible for publication or leaderboard display as a
clean pass when any query in the requested phase failed.

anti_patterns.instead: preserve diagnostics while changing pass/fail eligibility.

anti_patterns.why: the bug is the status contract

preserves.behavior: Fully successful runs still export and submit as clean passed results.
Query-level failure diagnostics remain visible in logs and result artifacts.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests -k 'partial and query and failure' -q
verifications.description: Targeted regression test proves query-level failures do not publish as clean passes.

work_units.notes:
W1 trace result (2026-05-03):
  - Core result construction is already detecting mixed query outcomes.
    `benchbox/core/results/builder.py:597` upgrades the result
    `validation_status` from `PASSED` to `PARTIAL` when measurement
    query failures are present; `tests/unit/core/results/test_builder.py:168`
    already covers this.
  - Schema-v2 export preserves the failure evidence. `benchbox/core/results/schema.py:272`
    recomputes measurement query totals from serialized query rows,
    `benchbox/core/results/schema.py:385` emits query error entries,
    and `summary.queries.failed` is included in the public bundle.
  - The pass/fail leak is downstream. `benchbox/cli/commands/run.py:1489`
    treats every status except `FAILED`/`INTERRUPTED` as a successful
    command, exports `PARTIAL` bundles, prints a green completion at
    `benchbox/cli/commands/run.py:1508`, and can still call
    `publish_bundle()` for those bundles at `benchbox/cli/commands/run.py:1514`.
  - `benchbox submit` loads the reconstructed query counts at
    `benchbox/cli/commands/submit.py:519` but only applies the existing
    TPC-DS compliance guard at `benchbox/cli/commands/submit.py:546`;
    it does not reject `failed_queries > 0`.
  - `benchbox publish`/`publish_bundle` similarly only guard unofficial
    compliance classes (`benchbox/cli/commands/publish.py:96` and
    `benchbox/cli/commands/publish.py:341`), so direct publication can
    still accept partial bundles.
  - Explorer ranking eligibility ignores status. `ManifestEntry` has
    `validation_status` but no failed-query count
    (`benchbox/core/explorer_pipeline/models.py:87`), and
    `is_ranking_eligible()` at `benchbox/core/explorer_pipeline/models.py:181`
    checks only trust label and visibility. The transformer extracts
    validation status at `benchbox/core/explorer_pipeline/transformer.py:189`
    but does not force failed-query bundles out of rankings.

W2 owned implementation files:
  - `benchbox/core/results/status.py` (new shared status/eligibility policy)
  - `benchbox/cli/commands/run.py`
  - `benchbox/cli/commands/submit.py`
  - `benchbox/cli/commands/publish.py`
  - `benchbox/core/explorer_pipeline/models.py`
  - `benchbox/core/explorer_pipeline/transformer.py`

W3 owned test files:
  - `tests/unit/cli/test_run_command_branches.py`
  - `tests/unit/cli/commands/test_submit.py`
  - `tests/unit/cli/commands/test_publish.py`
  - `tests/unit/core/explorer_pipeline/test_read_model_contract.py`
  - `tests/unit/core/explorer_pipeline/test_transformer.py`
work_units.summary: Trace the run-result status contract and list exact owned files
Make partial query failures explicit and non-clean-pass
